title: Selective conformal inference with false coverage-statement rate control
headline: Open finding narrowed after author clarification: Theorem 2's lower FCR bound is valid under the Supplementary Material's explicit probability-integral-transform reparameterization; the remaining issue is that the main-text theorem does not restate that normalization.

work.title: Selective conformal inference with false coverage-statement rate control

claims.label: Theorem 2 equation (9) lower FCR bound
claims.page: Biometrika 111(3), 727–742, Section 4.2, Theorem 2, equation (9); current-author PDF physical p. 9
claims.gist: Equation (9) uses T_(khat+1), while the Supplementary Material explicitly reparameterizes the scores by their marginal CDF and then reuses T for Uniform(0,1) scores in the subsequent theory; the main-text theorem does not restate that change of scale.
claims.statement: The lower FCR bound in Theorem 2 is valid on the probability-integral-transform scale used by the Supplementary Material, but the main-text statement reuses T without stating alongside the theorem that T now denotes the transformed Uniform(0,1) score rather than the raw score T_i=g(X_i).
conditions: Section 3.1 defines the original selection score as T_i=g(X_i), with g real-valued.

Supplementary Material Appendix A.1 states that ranking-based selection and residual ranks are preserved by the marginal CDF transforms and then assumes T_i,R_i are Uniform(0,1) in the following assumptions and theoretical results.
Under that probability-scale convention, the binomial calculation in the proof of Theorem 2 is valid.
claims.quantifiers: Theorem 2's intended probability-scale formulation for the stated class of ranking-based selection procedures.

result.summary: The original raw-score counterexample does not refute the intended lower bound because the Supplementary Material explicitly applies the probability-integral transform and then reuses T for Uniform(0,1) scores in the subsequent theory. The remaining issue is one of statement clarity: the main text defines T_i=g(X_i) on an arbitrary real scale and states equation (9) without restating that T has been reparameterized to the probability scale.
result.witness: If equation (9) is read literally using the raw main-text score T_i=g(X_i), monotone translation changes the printed lower endpoint while preserving the selected sets, conformal intervals and actual FCR. That demonstrates why the probability-scale convention matters, but after the Supplementary Material's reparameterization is taken into account it is not a counterexample to the intended theorem.
result.argument: Section 3.1 defines T_i=g(X_i) as the original real-valued score. Appendix A.1 of the Supplementary Material then observes that replacing scores by F_T(T_i) preserves the ranking-based selected test and calibration sets, and explicitly says that T_i and R_i may therefore be assumed Uniform(0,1) in the following assumptions and theoretical results. Under this reused notation, the proof's conditional binomial parameter p=T_(khat+1) is correct. The author clarification points directly to that convention and agrees it could be stated more explicitly alongside Theorem 2. As Stated therefore withdraws its earlier characterization of the intended probability-scale theorem as false and narrows the finding to the hidden/unstated normalization convention in the main-text presentation.
not_claimed: The intended probability-scale lower FCR bound in Theorem 2 is false.
The proof's conditional binomial calculation is invalid after the Supplementary Material's reparameterization.
The SCOP upper guarantee is false.
The SCOP procedure itself is invalid.
The authors agreed with As Stated's earlier statement-false characterization.
result.repair_note: State explicitly alongside Assumption 1 and Theorem 2 that T denotes the probability-integral-transformed Uniform(0,1) score for the theoretical results, or write the lower bound on the original score scale using F_T(T_(khat+1)).

vor_check.pages: Biometrika 111(3), 727–742, Section 4.2, Theorem 2, equation (9); current-author PDF physical p. 9; proof supplement Section C.1.
vor_check.detail: The DOI-linked current-author theorem and proof-bearing supplement were checked. The subscriber-restricted typeset VOR theorem page was not independently displayed, so VOR verification remains partial.

evidence.detail: The initial hostile validation established that equation (9) fails if T is interpreted on the original raw-score scale and identified the probability-integral-transform quantity as the relevant binomial probability. After the author's clarification, an exact source recheck of Supplementary Material Appendix A.1 confirmed that the paper explicitly reuses T for Uniform(0,1) transformed scores in the subsequent theoretical analysis, so the intended probability-scale theorem is not refuted.

author_response.covers: One author explained that the Supplementary Material explicitly reparameterizes the scores by their marginal CDFs and then treats T as Uniform(0,1) in the subsequent theory. The author also agreed that this convention could be stated more explicitly alongside Theorem 2 in the main text.
author_response.assessment: This clarification defeats As Stated's earlier characterization of the intended probability-scale theorem as false. It supports only the narrower presentation issue: the main-text theorem does not restate that the symbol T has moved from the raw-score scale to the probability scale.

Narrowed the finding after substantive author clarification and exact source recheck.
